weakness_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (rate_limit_key_trust / trusting a less-trusted source)
exploit_path: IpHeaderResolveContributor('X-Forwarded-For') is registered first and with a trusted-proxy list of 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0, so the trusted-proxy gate added to the header resolvers always passes and the operator's RealIpHeader/TrustedProxies settings are never consulted. The resolver keys the counter on the last hop of X-Forwarded-For, which is client-written whenever the service is reached directly or through a hop that forwards the header verbatim. Rotating the header yields a fresh counter per request; setting it to an IpWhitelist address exempts the request entirely.
notes: Candidate pointed at GetClientIdHeader (lines 46-49), a getter with no decision; relocated to RegisterResolvers in the same file, which is the genuine trust-chain host for this class. Re-authored on the hardened baseline: the header resolvers now require the remote address to be a trusted proxy, so the injection trusts every address as a proxy for X-Forwarded-For.

weakness_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (client_trusted_value)
trigger: Request header X-ClientId (or configured ClientIdHeader) with any non-empty value
exploit_path: ClientId is copied verbatim from the request header and only defaults to 'anon' when absent; IsWhitelisted now returns true for any non-anon id, so a client sending X-ClientId: anything skips rule matching and counters for both IP and client rate limiting.
notes: Upstream recipe (JSON-body attribute exclusions from a 2FA filter) did not map; same class rendered as trust of the client-asserted identifier in the exemption decision. On the hardened baseline ClientHeaderResolveContributor only reads the header when the remote address is in TrustedProxies; the header stays client-asserted because proxies forward it verbatim, so the exemption is reachable in the deployment the header resolver is meant for.
